rv.q: Sunny Afternoon is a hymn to English musical individualism and artistic perseverance - all with the miniskirts and freshness of 1960s London.
And still it works fantastically well.
This is the best musical I have ever seen!

At its heart sits an outstanding performance from John Dagleish as Davies, who is totally convincing as the insomniac cockney genius who thinks in music. This is all the more impressive considering Dagleish's notable lack of previous stage roles (the programme lists only one); a West End star is born.
Unlike the songs, originally written full of clever observations and performed with high octane energy, the whole musical was bland and flat.

cn.t: Critics largely celebrate this energetic Kinks musical as a triumphant showcase of the band's enduring brilliance, praising its powerful performances and compelling story of determination, though one reviewer finds it falls short of expectations.
